title: Slide 1 · Inference and proof traces
question: A graph explicitly lists C2 as a Camera. It also says all cameras are equipment. Which statement about C2 would require an inference if you answered from just these two records?
answer: C2 is equipment. Its camera type is already in the record. Connecting that type to the broader class takes one reasoning step.

title: Slide 2 · Make one inference
question: If R1 is applied twice to the same record, how many distinct eligibility facts about Ava exist?
answer: One. Both applications yield the same claim, Eligible(Ava). A set keeps one copy.

title: Slide 3 · Use one conclusion in the next rule
question: Suppose R2 is checked before R1 and just once. Which conclusion would the program miss?
answer: It would miss ready because eligible has not yet been added. A general forward-chaining procedure revisits affected rules until no new facts follow, assuming a finite set of possible facts in this example.

title: Slide 4 · Save the reasons along with the answer
question: Which original records must a clerk inspect at the leaves of this trace?
answer: The request by Ava for C1, Ava’s orientation record, and the availability record for C1. Eligible is an intermediate conclusion justified by R1.

title: Slide 5 · Find the first missing premise
question: Return to the complete proof on the preceding slide. If its C1 availability record was out of date, which conclusion needs checking?
answer: Inspect the availability premise and recompute any conclusion that used it. The rule application could have been valid for the recorded inputs even though one input was inaccurate.

title: Slide 6 · Name the evidence still needed
question: Replace this line: supported = {"requested", "eligible"} with: supported = {"available"} What will print?
answer:
['eligible', 'requested']
Only availability has support in this version. Sorting the two remaining requirements places eligible before requested.

title: Slide 8 · From this module to the next
question: A record confirms C1 came back. The only evidence about its cap is a blurry photo. Why would it help to record “the detector suggests a cap” separately from “a clerk saw a cap”?
answer: The first claim depends on an interpretation of the image. Keeping its source makes a later rule or clerk able to check it before treating the cap as confirmed.

title: Office hours · How does a proof help if someone typed in the wrong fact?
question: How does a proof help if someone typed in the wrong fact?
answer: It gives the desk a place to check. If a clerk challenges availability, follow Ready(Ava, C1) to the exact C1 record used by R2. A valid deduction tells us what follows from those premises. Checking the premises against the inventory is a separate task.

title: Office hours · Is a list of rule names enough to explain a decision?
question: Is a list of rule names enough to explain a decision?
answer: R1 and R2 could both be used for many borrowers and cameras. A useful trace identifies Ava, C1, the input records, and the intermediate Eligible(Ava) that connects the two steps. That lets a reviewer replay this particular decision.

title: Exercise 1
question: A trace lists R2, Requested(Ava, C1), Eligible(Ava), and Available(C2). Identify the precise error.
answer: R2 needs Available(C1) for this request. The supplied C2 fact has a different item, so the recorded premises do not justify Ready(Ava, C1).

title: Exercise 2
question: A rule engine checks R2 before R1 and finds no new ready request on its first check. Describe a stopping rule that works for this finite example.
answer: Keep applying the rules in passes. Stop only when an entire pass adds no new fact. After R1 supplies Eligible(Ava), a later pass gives R2 its missing premise.

title: Exercise 3
question: A message to Ava says “The system approved your loan.” The trace ends in Ready(Ava, C1). Rewrite the message using only what the trace supports.
answer: “Your request for C1 is ready for desk review. We found your request, your camera orientation record, and C1’s availability record.” The trace has no completed approval or handoff step.

title: Lab case 1 · Complete chain
question: Build the shortest chain to Ready(Ava, C1) using these rules.
answer: R1 uses Oriented(Ava) to derive Eligible(Ava). R2 combines that intermediate conclusion with Requested(Ava, C1) and Available(C1) to derive Ready(Ava, C1).

title: Lab case 2 · Wrong item
question: Which step still works, and which premise prevents the next one?
answer: R1 still derives Eligible(Ava). Ava requested C1, so R2 requires Available(C1). The availability record for C2 cannot supply it.

title: Lab case 3 · Independent evidence
question: Can the desk still justify ready? Which trace survives?
answer: Yes. R2 can use the directly verified Eligible(Ava) with the request and availability. A trace through R1 has lost its orientation premise. The direct eligibility record gives a separate route.

title: Module overview · Inference and proof traces
question: What is this module about?
answer: Inference and proof traces. Derive a conclusion from a small set of rules and reconstruct the evidence and intermediate steps that support it.
